### DealTimeline

Vertical deal lifecycle: funded, started, first distribution, settlement in progress, next distribution, final repayment plus profit; amounts only on money moments and exactly one active stage.

Level: organism · Contains: TimelineRow, TimelineNode

Use when:
- Deal page or investment detail showing where the deal is
- Money moments with amounts and expected dates

Don't use when:
- For paid/late status of individual payouts use Payouts cell or StatusPill
- For process steps the user completes use Stepper

Accessibility: Ordered list; announce completed/active/upcoming state per stage.

Compliance: Future stages show «متوقع»; never present expected dates or amounts as confirmed.

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

DealTimeline shows an investor where a deal is in its lifecycle: what has happened, what’s underway, and what’s still to come - with the money moments (distributions, repayment) called out by amount.

It is a composition, not a new primitive: each stage is a TimelineRow with an instance-swapped TimelineNode for its state. All shape, colour and connector logic is inherited from the 04i Timeline.

### Anatomy

A vertical stack of TimelineRow instances. Each row = a TimelineNode (marker + connectors) on the reading-start side, plus title, date, optional description and optional amount.

### Row parts

- TimelineNode - the marker + connector line; its State drives the colour/icon.
- Title - the milestone name (e.g. “First distribution”).
- Date - settlement / expected date; add “- Day N” or “expected” as context.
- Amount - shown only on money moments (funding, distributions, repayment).
- Connectors - first row has none above, last row has none below.

### Stages - the deal lifecycle

Six stages, in order:

- Deal funded - capital committed (amount).
- Project started - deal goes live.
- First distribution - first periodic payout (amount).
- Settlement in progress - active stage, shows elapsed days.
- Second distribution - upcoming payout (amount, “expected”).
- Final repayment + profit - capital + profit returned (amount, “expected”).

### States

Each stage’s TimelineNode carries one state:

- Completed - green filled + check; a finished stage.
- Active - larger solid green dot; the stage in progress now.
- Upcoming - hollow / muted; not yet reached.
- Skipped - muted, available for stages that don’t apply.

### Direction - LTR and RTL

RTL (Arabic) is primary; LTR mirrors it. The node column sits on the reading-start side, amounts on the far side.

LTR

RTL

### Code examples

Feed an ordered list of stages; the component derives connectors and “active”.

```typescript
<DealTimeline
  dir="rtl"
  stages={[
    { title: "Deal funded",      date: "2026-01-12", amount: 50000, state: "completed" },
    { title: "Project started",   date: "2026-01-20",                state: "completed" },
    { title: "First distribution",date: "2026-03-15", amount: 12500, state: "completed" },
    { title: "Settlement",        date: "2026-06-07", note: "Day 45", state: "active" },
    { title: "Second distribution",date:"2026-09-15", amount: 12500, state: "upcoming" },
    { title: "Final repayment",   date: "2027-01-12", amount: 37500, state: "upcoming" },
  ]}
/>
```

### Usage - Do and Don't

Keep it a single ordered journey with one clear present moment.

Do

Order stages chronologically and mark exactly one as active - the investor’s single “you are here”.

Do

Show amounts only on money moments (funding, distributions, repayment); leave milestones amount-free.

Don’t

Don’t mark multiple stages active, or show them out of order - the sequence is the whole point.

Don’t

Don’t use DealTimeline for non-sequential status (paid / late / pending) - that’s the Payouts cell or a StatusPill.

### Notes from the maintainer

Carrying-forward notes:

> **Tip:** DealTimeline is a composition - extend it by feeding stages, not by forking TimelineRow. Any node/connector change belongs in 04i.

> **Info:** Exactly one stage should be active; everything before it completed, everything after upcoming. The connector greening follows from the states, not the other way around.

> **Info:** Amounts appear only on money moments. Milestones (funded, started, settlement) run amount-free so the payouts stand out.
